stem_book: Observe the following statements. Assertion (A): The general solution of sin x = −1 is nπ + (−1)^(n) (3π/2). Reason (R): The principal value of sin x = K lies in [−π/2, π/2]. (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A (b) Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A (c) A is true but R is false (d) A is false but R is true
key: c A is true but R is false
derived: b if principal value = numerically least angle (book p.1 method, used by the key of M11L1V5Q10); c if principal value = solution in [0, 2π) (book p.1 definition)
reason: A is true, but whether R is true depends on which of the book's two conflicting definitions of 'principal value' is meant (numerically least ⇒ R true ⇒ b; in [0, 2π) ⇒ R false ⇒ c); the book's own keys use both, so no unique answer as printed.
work: nπ + (−1)^(n)·3π/2: n even ⇒ 2mπ + 3π/2, n odd ⇒ 2mπ − π/2, all with sin = −1 ⇒ A true; R true only under the numerically-least convention
